tasks.short: Review transcripts against requirements and write recommendation letters.

steps.what: Read the graduation and college entrance requirements that apply to these students.
inputs: the student's programme
requirements card when the programme office has written one
outputs: the requirements that apply to these students

steps.what: Read the transcripts for the courses, marks and credits of these students.
inputs: the requirements that apply to these students
the student-record transcript
outputs: the courses, marks and credits read

steps.what: Decide which graduation or entrance requirements these students meet, and record that result.
inputs: the requirements that apply to these students
the courses, marks and credits read
outputs: the recorded result of which requirements are met

steps.what: Write the letter of recommendation and give it to the named recipient.
inputs: the recorded result of which requirements are met
what the counselor knows of the student
outputs: the letter of recommendation given to the recipient

tasks.design: The programme office keeps a requirements card: programme, requirement, subject or course code, minimum mark, and credits. The counselor reads that card, or the prospectus when a row is missing, then reads the transcript in the student-record system and records which requirements are met. The counselor writes the recommendation letter and gives it to the named recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rules sat in a long prospectus, so each review started by hunting for the lines that apply to this student.
tasks.enabler_now: The programme office already knows the rules. Writing them once on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: A missing course code, a borderline mark, or an exemption is still the counselor's decision. The letter is still their words, given by them.
tasks.human_edge: Judging a borderline mark or an exemption, and writing a recommendation that is true of this student.
tasks.altitude: Finding a standard requirement is shorter when the card is current. The counselor still decides, still records the result, and still writes and gives every letter.

reach.task: Keep the requirements card for each programme
reach.learn: To check the course code and the minimum mark, and to tell the counselor when a rule changed

evidence.claim: A counselor compares a transcript with published graduation or entrance rules and writes the recommendation in their own words. A card can shorten the search for the rule. It does not make the decision or the letter. Model knowledge.
Whether these students meet a graduation or entrance requirement is not left to automated processing alone. The counselor decides and records it.

assumptions: The boundary is one student and one programme. Reading the transcript, deciding, recording the result, and writing and giving the letter each keep their full time.

Requirements card fields are programme, requirement, subject or course code, minimum mark, and credits. The producer is the programme office, when a rule changes. If a row is missing, the counselor reads the prospectus inside the lookup, before the decision.
The student-record system already stores the transcript the counselor reads today. This task adds no capture of courses, marks, or credits, and it adds no send, alert, or filled form.
The counselor does not rewrite the card. That upkeep is the programme office's 1.5 hours per 100 counselor hours on this task. The counselor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a programme office will keep the card, or the counselor is the only person who holds the prospectus.
Whether course codes on the transcript match the codes the programme office uses.
research_questions: Of the requirement checks on this desk, how many are a straight code-and-mark match, and how many turn on an exemption or a borderline mark?

incremental.description: The counselor adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The programme office rewrites the requirements card when a rule, a code, or a minimum mark changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the card has no course code, the counselor reads the prospectus inside the lookup, so most of that step remains. The transcript, the decision, the record, and the letter stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage students to explore opportunities and persevere.

steps.what: Prepare by reading which learning opportunities fit these students' later educational step.
inputs: the student's next educational step
opportunity card when a learning colleague has written one
outputs: the learning opportunities to raise, or none

steps.what: Encourage students to explore those learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks.
inputs: the learning opportunities to raise, or none
how the student is meeting the challenging tasks
outputs: what the student was encouraged to try

tasks.design: A learning colleague keeps an opportunity card: name, level, start, and who it suits. The counselor reads that card before the talk, or searches when the next step is not on it. In the room the counselor still encourages the student to explore and to persevere. The talk is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitable courses and placements sat in separate notes, so preparing for the talk meant a search each time.
tasks.enabler_now: The learning colleague already knows the current list. One card needs no new system.
tasks.still_hard: Encouraging this student, and judging what they can persevere with, stays in the room. A missing row puts the search back.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing what this student can face, and encouraging them without taking the choice away.
tasks.altitude: Preparing a standard opportunity is shorter when the card is current. The counselor still holds the conversation and gains no new decision.

reach.task: Keep the opportunity card for the next educational steps
reach.learn: To date the card, and to expect the counselor to search when the student's step is not listed

evidence.claim: Encouraging a student to explore and to persevere is a conversation. A list of opportunities can shorten the look-up before the talk. It does not shorten the talk. Model knowledge.
Recording this counseling conversation would record the counselor as well as the student, and that needs works-council consent. The talk is not recorded.

assumptions: The boundary is one student in the room. Encouraging stays in person and keeps its full time.

Opportunity card fields are name, level, start, and who it suits. The producer is a learning colleague, when an opportunity opens or closes. If the card has no row, the counselor searches inside the prepare step, before the talk.
Nothing is sent to the student. The counselor speaks the encouragement. The talk is not recorded, so no consent step is added.
The counselor does not rewrite the card. That upkeep is the learning colleague's 1 hour per 100 counselor hours on this task. The counselor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether anyone besides the counselor keeps a current list of learning opportunities.
How often the next step is absent from that list.
research_questions: Of the talks that encourage a student to persevere, how many depend on a named opportunity, and how many are only about the task in front of them?

incremental.description: The counselor adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the prepare step.
The learning colleague rewrites the opportunity card when a course or placement opens or closes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The card often has no row for this student's next step, so the prepare step stays long. Encouraging the student in the room is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate abilities, interests and personality from tests and interviews.

steps.what: Interview students or individuals about abilities, interests and personality characteristics.
inputs: why this student is being evaluated
outputs: what the student said about abilities, interests and personality

steps.what: Read tests, records and professional sources on those abilities, interests and personality characteristics.
inputs: what the student said about abilities, interests and personality
score card when the test administrator has written one
records and professional sources
outputs: the scores and source lines read

steps.what: Evaluate those abilities, interests and personality characteristics, and record the evaluation.
inputs: what the student said about abilities, interests and personality
the scores and source lines read

tasks.design: The counselor interviews the student and does not record the interview. The test administrator writes a score card: test name, date, scale, score, and who scored it. The counselor reads that card, or the full report when the card is missing, together with the records and professional sources, and writes the evaluation. The counselor's written evaluation is the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores sat inside long test reports, so each evaluation started by hunting for the scale and the score.
tasks.enabler_now: The test administrator already scores the test. Copying five fields onto a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: What the scores mean for this student, next to the interview, is still the counselor's judgement. The interview stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Putting the interview together with the scores, and refusing a reading the sources do not support.
tasks.altitude: Finding a score is shorter when the card is there. The counselor still interviews, still evaluates, and still writes the evaluation.

reach.task: Write the score card when a test is scored
reach.learn: To include the scale and who scored it, and to leave the full report available when the card is not enough

evidence.claim: A counselor interviews the student and reads tests, records, and professional sources before writing an evaluation. A score card can shorten the hunt inside a long report. It does not make the evaluation. Model knowledge.
The evaluation of abilities, interests, and personality is not left to automated processing alone. The counselor writes it.
Recording the interview would record the counselor as well as the student, and that needs works-council consent. The interview is not recorded.

assumptions: The boundary is one student. The interview and the written evaluation keep their full time. Only the reading of scores is shorter, and only when the card exists.

Score card fields are test name, date, scale, score, and who scored it. The producer is the test administrator, when the test is scored. If the card is missing, the counselor reads the full report inside that same step. The counselor does not treat the card as the evaluation.
No process writes the evaluation, sends it, or raises an alert from a score. The counselor writes the evaluation by hand.

The counselor does not rewrite score cards. That upkeep is the test administrator's 1.5 hours per 100 counselor hours on this task. The counselor's own upkeep is zero. Access to existing test records is checked before rollout; no new store of scores is added.
unknowns: Whether test administrators will write the five fields, or scores stay only inside the full report.
Whether any test used here is treated as health data under national rules.
research_questions: How often is the score the counselor needs already on the front of the report, and how often is it buried in an appendix?

incremental.description: The counselor adds no recurring chore. Reading the score card is the source step.
The test administrator writes the score card when a test is scored.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Score cards are often missing, so the counselor reads the full report. The interview and the written evaluation stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell students about programmes, aid, trades and apprenticeships.

steps.what: Look up college degree programs, admission requirements, financial aid opportunities, trade and technical schools, and apprenticeship programs.
inputs: the topic the student asked about
programme catalogue when the career-information officer has written one
outputs: the rows or source pages that match the question

steps.what: Provide students with that information and say which of those topics fit.
inputs: the rows or source pages that match the question
outputs: what the student was told, including what was not on the catalogue

tasks.design: A career-information officer keeps a catalogue: topic, name, admission requirements, deadline, source, and last checked date, for degree programmes, financial aid, trade and technical schools, and apprenticeships. The counselor looks up the question there, or in the source when the row is missing or stale, then tells the student which parts fit. The counselor speaks that information. Nothing replies in their place.
tasks.previous_blocker: Admission rules, aid, and apprenticeship facts sat on separate pages, so each question started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: Those facts are public and already collected by a career-information officer. One catalogue page needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Saying which fact fits this student, and noticing a stale date, stays with the counselor. A missing row is a search again.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what fits this student's question, and refusing to state an admission rule the source does not show.
tasks.altitude: A standard lookup is shorter when the catalogue row is current. The counselor still tells the student and still decides what fits.

reach.learn: To date each row, and to leave the source named so the counselor can open it when the row is stale

evidence.claim: Counselors answer questions about degree programmes, admission rules, aid, trade schools, and apprenticeships from published pages. A dated catalogue can shorten that search. The counselor still tells the student what fits. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one student and one question. Telling the student, and saying what fits, stays in person and keeps its full time.

Catalogue fields are topic, name, admission requirements, deadline, source, and last checked date. The producer is the career-information officer, when a page changes. If the row is missing or the date is old, the counselor reads the source inside the lookup, before telling.
The catalogue quotes published facts. It does not write advice, send a message, or alert anyone. The counselor tells the student.
The counselor does not rewrite the catalogue. That upkeep is the career-information officer's 2 hours per 100 counselor hours on this task. The counselor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a career-information officer exists here, or the counselor collects these pages alone.
How often the questions are about a programme the catalogue does not list.
research_questions: Of the questions students ask about programmes, aid, trades, and apprenticeships, how many are answered from a page that was checked this term?

incremental.description: The counselor adds no recurring chore. Reading the catalogue is the lookup step.
The career-information officer updates the catalogue when a programme, an aid rule, a school, or an apprenticeship changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Many questions have no current catalogue row, so the counselor still opens the source. Telling the student what fits stays at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The counselor still decides whether a student meets a requirement, still writes and gives each recommendation, still encourages in the room, still interprets tests, and still tells the student what fits. A current card only shortens the search for a rule, a score, or a published fact.
reach: A programme officer learns to keep programme, requirement, subject or course code, minimum mark, and credits on the requirements card before a transcript review.
A test administrator learns to write test name, date, scale, score, and who scored it before the counselor evaluates.
A career-information officer learns to date each catalogue row and name its source before the counselor tells a student.
skills_to_grow: Read the requirements card and still open the prospectus when a course code is missing.
Record the requirement result and the evaluation in their own words, and do not treat a score card as the evaluation.
Tell the student only the catalogue facts that are dated, and say when a row is missing.
role.ambitious_version: The counselor still makes every requirement decision, every evaluation, and every recommendation. The cards do not decide, write, or tell.

job.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
